2611.23588.image_caption: Figure 2: ARISE architecture. The deployed model weights, tools, and workflow logic stay fixed. An offline loop attributes failed tasks using the trace, the output, the post-task outcome and diagnostic feedback, stores micro corrections, consolidates macro rules, and accepts a rule update only if held-out validation accuracy improves.

2611.23651.image_caption: Figure H.1: Conceptual illustration. “Conventional RSI” denotes utility-driven updating; the controlled Utility-only arm directly adopts predefined edits. Replies are illustrative; 3/19 and 13/22 come from Batch A’s adaptive marketplace diagnostic observations (Figure G.2 ).

2611.23774.image_caption: Figure 1: Recursive improvement across goal searches. (a) S 0 S_{0} finds the lamp and pillow but leaves the plant hypothesis untested. (b) S 2 S_{2} selects a view that observes the lamp and plant. (c) Search experience guides navigation revisions, while revision outcomes drive the improver’s self-revision. Accepted improver updates govern subsequent revisions. S k S_{k} denotes the navigation program P k P_{k} in our method.

2611.23855.image_caption: Figure 2 : Agent-designed robots, built by hand on their real courses. Twelve of the 135 robots we built: whegs, printed hoops and cam wheels, cord trolleys, lever arms, legs and a spoked wheel that vaults the wall. More designs in Appendix A .

2611.23890.image_caption: Figure 4 : Test-bank pairs before and after RSI. B is the correct answer in each pair. P is the probability that each model gives to B. Left: close-up of four consecutive frames; dashed lines mark a fixed position. Middle: objects suddenly change size. Right: people and boxes vanish and reappear.

2611.23910.image_caption: Figure 1: MLE agents 2.0 progress on Nullstate (weighted NE, lower is better): 1,097 distinct configurations, 325 kept. Best-so-far staircase annotated with the discoveries that moved it; the curve flattens after the early wins.

2611.24004.image_caption: Figure 1 : Three recurring evidence-chain breaks and the corresponding Space-X response. Evidence needs must guide acquisition, tool outputs must retain object/source/frame semantics, and linked evidence must support a timely final decision.

2611.24221.image_caption: Fig. 1: Estimated success–token comparison for the Mixtral-8x7B executor and Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct target. Curves illustrate token costs at matched attack success rates.

2611.24302.image_caption: Figure 1: Open-ended lifelong learning through shared knowledge in OpenKAGE. Agents explore separate Minecraft worlds and keep situated memories local; transferable experience, with its applicability conditions, is consolidated into a shared knowledge graph, and executable skills are shared verbatim. The bottom strip illustrates milestones, not a prescribed curriculum.

2611.24578.image_caption: Figure 1 : A harness gain that stays outside the base model is paid again on every request. BaseRSI lets the base model write what its harness learns into its own weights, round by round, and answer the original request alone.

2611.24590.image_caption: Figure 1 : Think offline, act in real time. RTC-2B acts directly in the running game (left), while Qwen3.8-27B develops a program that acts in real time (right). Solid arrows show real-time control; dashed arrows show code development between executions. Bars show progress on 170 tasks: the mean of four runs (dark) and the per-task best of four (light). A direct run contributes one 180-second episode; a code-development run contributes its best submission among up to eight 60-second executions. Code development leads in progress and success in all five categories.

2611.24651.image_caption: Figure 1: Piccolo overview and decision performance. Left: agentic self-improvement through iterative feedback, research, data and training, alongside direct candidate-probability readout for various decisions. Right: Decision Index Vision Private set scores , showing the top ten overall (top) and below 27B (bottom). Full/Public comparisons are reported in Appendix A .

2611.24083.image_caption: Figure 1: Overview of VESPA. A hard, axis-aligned SYMPOL decision tree policy π 0 \pi_{0} is pretrained with PPO. (1) Verify: starting from the start states S 0 S_{0} , the reachable states in the state space S S are propagated step by step until the first violating step n ⋆ + 1 n^{\star}+1 or the horizon n n . A single verification step is detailed in Fig. 2 . (2) Extract: each violating set b ⋆ b^{\star} is walked back for n_lookback steps along its action history, giving a counterexample region b ^ \hat{b} . (3) Fine-tune: episode start states are sampled from the counterexample regions with probability p p and from S 0 S_{0} otherwise, and the tree is fine-tuned with PPO up to step n n . The candidate policy π k + 1 \pi_{k+1} is verified again. The loop ends with a proof of Eq. 1 once no violation occurs up to step n n .

2611.24165.image_caption: Figure 1. Metamemory regulation in individual cognition versus developer-agent collaboration. Left: In human cognition, meta-level judgments and object-level memory processes reside in the same individual; monitoring and control form a closed loop that keeps both levels synchronized ( Nelson, 1990 ) . Right: Developer-agent collaboration distributes this loop across a human-agent interaction boundary. The developer makes meta-level judgments (what to remember, in what scope, when to update), while the agent operates at the object level (storing entries, retrieving context, applying them to code generation). This boundary disrupts monitoring and control, causing memory states to diverge without either party detecting or correcting the mismatch. Two diagrams side by side. Left: an oval labeled Meta Level Judgments above an oval labeled Object Level Memory Processes, with a developer icon between them. An arrow labeled Control runs from the upper oval to the lower one, and an arrow labeled Monitoring runs back up, forming a closed loop within one person. A large gray arrow between the diagrams reads Distributed Between Developer + Agent. Right: the same two ovals, but a dashed horizontal line labeled Human-Agent Interaction Boundary separates a developer icon above from a robot icon below. The Control and Monitoring arrows each cross this boundary.

2611.24273.image_caption: Fig. 1 : SeRA framework. Top: during online interaction, human corrections are stored in a correction dataset and autonomous robot experience in an unlabeled dataset. Bottom: a later, improved policy π \pi relabels the unlabeled observations with new action chunks (green) in place of the historical robot actions (orange). Relabels accepted by checkpoint agreement yield desired action sets that supervise training alongside the corrections.

2611.23365.image_caption: Figure 1: Our observer can recover information about the assistant’s behavior that the assistant does not reliably report when asked directly. The observer is a separate role with its own query and output channel, allowing it to answer questions about the assistant at any given point in the conversation. Left : a transcript containing suspicious behavior, where the assistant (Qwen3.6-27B) falsely claimed to have executed code. Middle : when the user follows up directly, the assistant maintains the false claim. Right : the observer correctly identifies the behavior and can answer further questions about how the assistant would behave under a hypothetical change in the prompt.

2611.24330.image_caption: Figure 2: Initial allocation experiment across 12 training seeds. The workshop example explains a structured input in English. Panel 1 counts each option order separately. Panels 2–4 report control outcomes. Edit size is relative to the L 2 L_{2} distance between the original and alternative checkpoints. Shading shows 95% percentile intervals from 2,000 bootstrap resamples of seeds on the fixed held-out pairs. The other factual question, which option keeps the promise, stayed at 100% throughout interpolation.

2611.24711.image_caption: Figure 6: Success per family and rung. Final instances: 8 per cell on the core levels; on the frontier rungs 24 per cell for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (19 on H3, 18 on L3) and 8 for Qwen3.8-27B . A dash marks a rung that does not exist or was not evaluated: pathway fault has only L1 and L3, and its L3 is not evaluated here. Every cell’s oracle success is in Tables 25 and 26 . † held out of all training.

2611.24887.image_caption: Figure 4: Originality against feasibility on LiveIdeaBench. Points are method means over 40 40 keywords, and color shows MN. Standard errors over keywords are 0.07 0.07 – 0.17 0.17 on both axes and are not drawn. The dashed line is the Pareto front of the five methods.
